text:
Anya: quick heads-up — did an int4 bringup for halcyon-small against the wiki-short embed suite (queries <=8 tokens). recall@1 dropped ~6.2% vs fp16 baseline, which feels specific to short queries. posting raw numbers and what I ran.

Mike: can you paste the eval command and exact quant config?

Anya: sure — used the standard onboard script with per-channel symmetric quant + zero-point clamp disabled. command: 
```
python tools/eval_embeddings.py \
  --model halcyon-small:int4-perchannel \
  --dataset wiki-short \
  --batch-size 256 \
  --metrics recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,cosine_sim_stats \
  --num-workers 16
```
results: 
- fp16 baseline: r@1 0.842, r@5 0.967, mean sim 0.38
- int4 per-channel: r@1 0.780, r@5 0.960, mean sim 0.33
- int4 per-tensor: r@1 0.758, r@5 0.952, mean sim 0.29

Devon: interesting — the mean similarity drop and r@1 move suggest a small-scale collapse on short sequences. did you look at embedding norms?

Anya: yep. quick distribution: 
- fp16 mean L2 1.02, std 0.12
- int4 per-channel mean L2 0.67, std 0.09
so norms compressed a lot.

JL: that screams dynamic range miscalibration in the quant step. per-channel helps but still losing headroom for short queries. can you try a cheap re-calib where we collect activation mins/maxes on a small holdout and use a slightly higher percentile clip (e.g., 99.9 -> 99.99)?

Mike: also try enabling "scale-rescale" postprocessing we use for other compact models: multiply by learned per-dim scale from a 1k calibration set. quick command: 
```
# calibration run (collect stats)
python tools/collect_quant_stats.py --model halcyon-small --dataset wiki-cal --samples 1000 --out stats/halcyon_small_stats.npz

# re-quant with clip_percentile and rescale
python tools/quantize.py --model halcyon-small --stats stats/halcyon_small_stats.npz --clip 99.99 --per-channel --rescale True --out halcyon-small-int4-rescaled
```

Anya: re-ran with clip=99.99 + rescale True + clamp=3 (clamp is our kernel-level dynamic range guard). new numbers: r@1 0.811, r@5 0.964, mean sim 0.36. still a bit below fp16 but much better.

Devon: nice. can you also run a quick UMAP + silhouette on wiki-short to see cluster separability? if clusters merge, that'll explain r@1 drop.

Anya: did that real quick. silhouette: fp16 0.42, int4-rescaled 0.31. UMAP shows tighter blobs but more overlap for short tail categories. posted a tiny image gist: https://redwood.internal/g/halcyon-int4-umap (private).

JL: ok so two levers — better calibration / rescale and maybe a small architecture-aware bias correction (add per-dim bias after quant) — but that's heavier. operations-wise, can we patch the onboard recipe to default to per-channel+rescale for halcyon-small and require a short-query holdout check?

Mike: +1. also flag in eval dashboard to break down recall by query length buckets (<4, 4-8, >8). we missed that earlier.

Anya: I can open a PR to the quant recipes and add the extra eval bucket. will also attach the calibration script and the minimal repro.

deploy-bot: note created ticket INF-4282: "halcyon-small int4 short-query recall regression — add per-channel+rescale default and short-query holdout eval" assigned to @Anya.

Mike: awesome, thanks. :thumbsup:

JL: let's re-run on a few more languages if time permits — short queries often behave worse in non-en languages because tokenization changes.

Anya: will do next. thanks everyone. :pray:
